subject: Midrun OKR prioritization, tradeoffs, and QBR asks
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midrun OKR prioritization, tradeoffs, and QBR asks

Team —

We’re at the midrun checkpoint for Q3. In advance of the leadership QBR next week I want a concise set of asks so Execs can sign off quickly. High-level context and proposed shifts below. I’m marking owners and required external dependencies.

Top-level snapshot (TL;DR)
- KR1 (Throughput improvements): On-track but low confidence on hitting 2x cost-per-token reduction by EOY without additional infra work.
- KR2 (Latency SLA for hosted API): At risk; observed tail-latency regressions on long-context jobs in the past three sprints.
- KR3 (Enterprise Migrations): Progressing; procurement for CloudScale deal is the gating item.

Proposed midrun tradeoffs (ask Execs to approve if necessary):
1) Re-scope KR1 target from 2x to 1.6x for Q3, keep the engineering runway for a targeted kernel optimization in Q4. Owner: Vivek.
2) Move a non-user-facing perf experiment (batching research spike) from Q3 into a limited experiment-only track to reduce rollout risk. Owner: Vanessa.
3) For KR2, schedule a canary rollback and an ops escalation budget (2 FTE-weeks of SRE support) to stabilize tail latency. Owner: Priya/Aditya.

Immediate asks (what I need from each of you by EOD Wed):
- Vanessa: One-page tradeoffs doc for throttling vs. KV-caching adjustments; include top 3 config knobs and expected unit-cost impact.
- Vivek: Reproduce plan + quick mitigation timeline (48/72/1-week) for tail-latency regressions and whether Dedicated capacity buys us time.
- Aditya: Draft email to Procurement/CloudScale to accelerate the PO and confirm SOC2 evidence availability (attach SOW draft).
- Laura: Consolidate QBR slide deck outline and add a single slide with “approved tradeoff asks” for Exec sign-off.

External asks (CloudScale)
- Procurement contact and DocuSign link for PO execution (see attachments).
- SOC2 evidence: we need a copy of the technical penetration test report for their legal review by Friday.

Attachments: OKR-tracker-2026Q3.xlsx (current metrics), QBR-packet-draft.pdf (slide skeleton), SOW-proposal-cloudscale.docx (draft to send to CloudScale).

I’ll collect replies and circulate a single “Exec ask” slide by Thursday AM. If anyone anticipates missing the Wed EOD ask, reply with a one-line alternate ETA.

—
Priya Natarajan
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

On Mon, Aug 2, 2026 at 9:12 AM Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We’re at the midrun checkpoint for Q3...

Thanks Priya — I’ll take the tradeoffs doc. Quick notes:
- Throttling has good short-term ROI but risks higher 5xxs for bursty enterprise jobs.
- KV-caching changes look promising for 95th/99th but add memory pressure; need a canary on Dedicated first.

Deliverable: one-page tradeoffs doc + a table with expected unit-cost delta. ETA: Wed EOD. If we need to accelerate, I can share a reduced table by Wed noon.

Action items I’m blocking on: two extra GPU nodes to run the canary on Dedicated for a 24-36 hour window — Vivek, can you confirm availability?

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product (Performance) | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

On Mon, Aug 2, 2026 at 9:37 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Priya — I’ll take the tradeoffs doc.

I’ll own the repro and mitigation plan. Short answers for now:
- Can confirm capacity: we can allocate 2x A100 equivalent nodes for a 48-hour canary without impacting committed Dedicated customers, but it requires shifting a scheduled maintenance window (I’ll coordinate with infra).
- Mitigation timeline suggestion:
  * 48h: isolate regression root cause (config vs kernel); run KV/prefix-cache toggle test.
  * 72h: release temporary throttle + rollback path to previous kernel if no improvement.
  * 1 week: if rollback not acceptable, target a minimal kernel patch with prioritized unit tests.

One constraint: if we pull in Dedicated for an extended canary, we should notify CloudScale procurement (cost delta) and confirm billing alignment. Aditya — can you add this ask to your procurement outreach?

—
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Please prepare:
- Aditya: Procurement outreach to CloudScale (include PO timeline and SOC2 doc ask). Draft should be customer-facing and include the SOW attachment. I want to send to Sarah and ProcureOps by EOD today.

If you want, I can join the procurement thread to help push PO timelines.

Thanks for the clear summary, Priya. Quick responses from CloudScale side:
- Procurement: attaching PO path — ProcureOps will take the SOW and return a signed PO within 3 business days once we have the penetration test/ SOC2 report. See DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/CF-2039487
- SOC2 / penetration test: security has requested the most recent pen-test PDF and a short note on key remediations. We can accept work-in-progress artifacts but need a date for final delivery.
- Dedicated nodes: we can agree to a short canary window on our side, but please confirm any incremental cost and provide an MSA amendment if the Dedicated usage falls outside our current commitment.

ProcureOps (procure@cloudscale.com) will follow up with a more formal checklist. I’ll copy their PO coordinator on the next note.
